elements.quote: A systematic review of the literature was conducted by searching PubMed, the Excerpta Medica Database (Embase, via OvidSP), Scopus and Web of Science, covering publications from inception to April 2024.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states that a systematic review of the literature was conducted, identifying the report as a systematic review (with meta-analysis).

elements.quote: This meta-­ analysis aimed to evaluate the association between adherence to a Mediterranean diet and metabolic syndrome among children and adolescents.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit objective statement of the review's aim.

elements.quote: Studies were included if they evaluated the association between adherence to a Mediterranean diet and metabolic syndrome among children and adolescents.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main inclusion criteria (population, exposure, and outcome) but does not state any exclusion criteria, which the element description requires.

elements.quote: by searching PubMed, the Excerpta Medica Database (Embase, via OvidSP), Scopus and Web of Science, covering publications from inception to April 2024.
elements.reason: The abstract names the information sources (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science) and gives the search coverage date (inception to April 2024).
The abstract contains no statement about risk-of-bias assessment methods; risk-of-bias methodology (modified Newcastle-Ottawa scale) appears only in the body (text_11), not in the abstract.

elements.quote: A random-­ effects model was used to estimate the summary effect size.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the synthesis method used (random-effects meta-analysis to estimate the summary effect size).

elements.quote: A total of eight studies involving children and adolescents aged 6 to 19 years were included in the meta-­ analysis (n=6562, 50% girls).
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies (8), participants (n=6562), and relevant characteristics (age range 6-19 years, 50% girls).

elements.quote: Low adherence to the Mediterranean diet was associated with greater odds of metabolic syndrome than was medium/high adherence (odds ratio [OR] = 2.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.45 to 3.28; p < 0.001; inconsistency index [ I 2 ] = 64.15%).
elements.reason: The abstract presents the result for the main outcome (MetS) with effect estimate, CI, p-value, and heterogeneity; the accompanying studies (8) and participants (n=6562) are reported in the Results sentence.

elements.quote: odds ratio [OR] = 2.18, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.45 to 3.28; p < 0.001
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports the summary estimate (OR 2.18) with its 95% confidence interval (1.45 to 3.28).

elements.quote: Low adherence to the Mediterranean diet was associated with greater odds of metabolic syndrome than was medium/high adherence
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect and which comparison group is favored: low adherence is associated with greater odds of MetS relative to medium/high adherence.
The abstract does not summarize limitations of the evidence (e.g., risk of bias, inconsistency, cross-sectional design); limitations are discussed only in the body of the paper (text_20).

elements.quote: This meta-­ analysis suggested that increased adherence to a Mediterranean diet is associated with lower probabilities of having cardiometabolic risk among children and adolescents. Thus, our findings suggest that public health strategies are needed to implement and promote effective actions toward healthy eating habits in children and adolescents.
elements.reason: The abstract's conclusion provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications for public health strategies.
The abstract does not mention any funding source for the review, and no funding information appears anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
The abstract does not provide a registration name or number; registration (PROSPERO CRD42022343383) is reported only in the Methods section (text_5), not in the abstract.

elements.quote: Background The Mediterranean diet has been associated with improved metabolic health among adults. This meta-­ analysis aimed to evaluate the association between adherence to a Mediterranean diet and metabolic syndrome among children and adolescents.
elements.reason: The abstract background briefly notes existing knowledge (benefit in adults) and implies an uncertainty gap for children/adolescents, but no dedicated Introduction/rationale text describing the current state of knowledge and uncertainties was retrieved.
No retrieved evidence explicitly explains the importance of or need for conducting this review; the abstract conclusion mentions public health strategies but not the rationale for the review itself.
No retrieved evidence discusses prior similar systematic reviews or explains the need for an update/replication relative to existing reviews.
This is a review of the association between diet adherence and metabolic syndrome, not a review of intervention effects, so a mechanism of intervention action does not apply.
This is not a review of complex interventions or delivery contexts, so a logic model requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: To be eligible for inclusion in the present review, studies needed to meet the following criteria: (i) were children or adolescents aged 5-19 years, all countries and ethnic backgrounds; (ii) had a MetS outcome; (iii) had an adherence to the MedDiet assessed by a validated questionnaire; and (iv) had a longitudinal and cross-­ sectional study design.
elements.reason: Population (age 5-19, all countries), outcome (MetS), exposure (validated MedDiet questionnaire), and eligible study designs are explicitly specified.

elements.quote: we restricted our inclusion criteria to studies published in English
elements.reason: Language restriction is mentioned, but only in the Discussion as a limitation; no dissemination year range or publication status criteria are reported in the Methods/eligibility criteria.
No distinction is made between excluding studies because outcomes were not measured versus outcomes not reported.

elements.quote: Children and adolescents with low adherence to the MedDiet had greater odds of developing MetS compared to those with medium to high adherence.
elements.reason: Comparison groups for the synthesis (low vs medium-to-high MedDiet adherence) are implied by the results, but grouping rules for the synthesis are not explicitly specified in the Methods or linked to review objectives.

elements.quote: However, to narrow the scope of the meta-­ analysis, only studies that associated the MedDiet with the outcome of MetS were included.
elements.reason: A rationale is given for restricting inclusion to studies associating MedDiet with MetS (to narrow the meta-analysis scope).

elements.quote: The searches included studies published from database inception to 22 April 2024.
elements.reason: The last search date (22 April 2024) is explicitly reported for the databases searched.

elements.quote: Excerpta Medica Database (Embase, via OvidSP), Scopus, Web of Science and PubMed. The searches included studies published from database inception to 22 April 2024.
elements.reason: Database names are reported with coverage from inception to 22 April 2024, and a platform (OvidSP) is given for Embase, but search interfaces/platforms for Scopus, Web of Science and PubMed are not specified.
No study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories were reported as searched (PROSPERO registration is protocol registration, not a study source).
No websites, search engines, or other online sources were reported as searched.
No organisations or manufacturers were reported as contacted to identify studies.
No individuals were contacted to identify studies; author contact (text_10) concerned missing data, not study identification.

elements.quote: The reference lists of eligible studies were manually examined to find further relevant papers and included if suitable.
elements.reason: The type of reference lists examined (reference lists of eligible studies) is specified.
No backward or forward citation searching was reported.
No journals or conference proceedings were consulted directly as sources.

elements.quote: The complete search strategies used for all the databases are presented in online supplemental file 2.
elements.reason: Full search strategies are reported in a supplemental file rather than in the manuscript, and the in-text description gives only example terms, not the complete strings as run for each database.

elements.quote: The search was limited to peer-­ reviewed studies published in English.
elements.reason: Limits (English language, peer-reviewed, date to 22 April 2024) are described, but no justification linking them to the eligibility criteria is provided.
No published search filters or hedges are cited, and no adaptations of such filters are described.
No evidence that natural-language processing or text-analysis tools were used to identify or refine search terms.
No evidence that translation tools were used to translate search strings between sources.
No validation of the search strategy is described.

elements.quote: A professional librarian was consulted to ensure the quality of the search strategy.
elements.reason: Consultation with a librarian is reported, but no formal peer review process or tool (e.g., PRESS) is described.

elements.quote: The search strategy included controlled vocabulary terms specific to each database along with keywords derived from scoping index articles relevant to this meta-­ analysis.
elements.reason: The search appears conceptually structured (exposure and outcome terms described); no indication that a non-PICO structure was used requiring further description.

elements.quote: Two authors (VPD and AG-­H) thoroughly examined the entire texts of identified publications for eligibility after removing duplicates and systematically reviewed the titles and abstracts of eligible manuscripts.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers (two named authors) is reported for both title/abstract screening and full-text examination.

elements.quote: Two authors (VPD and AG-­H) thoroughly examined the entire texts of identified publications for eligibility
elements.reason: Two reviewers screened each stage, but the text does not explicitly state that they worked independently during title/abstract or full-text screening (independence is stated only for the searches in text_7).

elements.quote: In case of discrepancies or uncertainty regarding eligibility, a third reviewer (CA-­S) was consulted to reach consensus.
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution via consultation with a third reviewer to reach consensus is described.

elements.quote: In cases where missing information was identified in the published paper, the relevant authors of those studies were contacted directly to request the missing information.
elements.reason: Contacting authors is described only for missing data during data extraction, not for obtaining or confirming eligibility information during study selection.

elements.quote: The search was limited to peer-­ reviewed studies published in English.
elements.reason: The search was restricted to English-language publications, so no translation of abstracts or articles was required.

elements.quote: 1565 were classified as ineligible by automation tools
elements.reason: Automation tools are mentioned as having removed records, but the methods do not describe how these tools were integrated into the selection process.
No evidence of externally derived classifiers being used in the selection process.
No evidence of internally derived classifiers being used in the selection process.
No evidence of machine-learning prioritisation tools or screening stopping rules being used.
No evidence of crowdsourcing platforms being used in study selection.
No evidence of previously screened datasets being used to eliminate records.

elements.quote: The extracted data were systematised via a specially constructed standardised data extraction form (see study protocol), and the extracted data were then reviewed for consistency by the reviewers.
elements.reason: Data extraction by 'the reviewers' (plural) is implied, but the exact number of reviewers collecting data from each report is not explicitly stated.
Independence is stated only for critical appraisal ('Each included study was independently reviewed for critical appraisal'), not for the data collection/extraction process itself.

elements.quote: Consensus was used to settle disagreements; the results are shown in table 1.
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution via consensus is described, though in the context of appraisal/data review.

elements.quote: In cases where missing information was identified in the published paper, the relevant authors of those studies were contacted directly to request the missing information.
elements.reason: Process for obtaining missing data from study investigators is explicitly described.
No automation tools are reported as being used for data collection/extraction; automation tools mentioned relate only to screening (text_15).

elements.quote: The search was limited to peer-­ reviewed studies published in English.
elements.reason: Only English-language studies were included, so no translation methods were needed.
No evidence that data were extracted from figures, so no software specification is required.

elements.quote: Studies were also excluded if they presented duplicate data from the same source and year. When two studies used duplicate data from the same source and year, the study with the larger sample size was selected.
elements.reason: Decision rule for selecting among multiple reports of the same data is described.

elements.quote: The following information was extracted from the included studies: (a) reference (year); (b) country; (c) characteristics of the subjects, including total sample size, sex ratio, age range and mean age; (d) type of questionnaire used; and (e) outcome information, including information on MetS and adherence to the MedDiet.
elements.reason: Outcome domains (MetS and MedDiet adherence) are listed, but they are not formally defined in the data items section; definitions (e.g., IDF criteria) appear only in results.
No time frame of measurement for outcomes is specified anywhere in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: All results from each study that were compatible with each outcome domain were included.
elements.reason: Explicitly states that all compatible results within each outcome domain were sought.
All compatible results were sought, so no selection process was needed.
No evidence of changes to outcome definitions is reported; conditional element does not apply.
No evidence of changes to result-selection processes is reported; conditional element does not apply.
No statement identifies which outcomes were considered most important for interpreting conclusions or a rationale for prioritisation.

elements.quote: The following information was extracted from the included studies: (a) reference (year); (b) country; (c) characteristics of the subjects, including total sample size, sex ratio, age range and mean age; (d) type of questionnaire used; and (e) outcome information, including information on MetS and adherence to the MedDiet.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists and defines the variables sought, including participant characteristics, exposure assessment tool, and outcome information.

elements.quote: In cases where missing information was identified in the published paper, the relevant authors of those studies were contacted directly to request the missing information.
elements.reason: The authors describe contacting study authors for missing data, but no assumptions made about missing or unclear information (e.g., imputation or default assumptions) are described.

elements.quote: The extracted data were systematised via a specially constructed standardised data extraction form (see study protocol)
elements.reason: A specially constructed data extraction form is mentioned, but no cited tool or guideline used to determine which data items to collect is reported.

elements.quote: a modified version of the Newcastle Ottawa cohort scale was used for cross-­ sectional research (online supplemental file 1)
elements.reason: The risk-of-bias tool (modified Newcastle-Ottawa scale) is explicitly named.

elements.quote: Selection | Comparability | Outcome | Statistical ... Representativeness of the sample | Sample size | Non-­ respondents | Ascertainment of exposure | Based on design and analysis | Assessment of outcome | test
elements.reason: The domains/items of the modified NOS are shown in Table 1 (Selection, Comparability, Outcome, Statistical test with sub-items).
No overall risk-of-bias judgement or rules for deriving it are reported; Table 1 shows item-level ratings only.

elements.quote: a modified version of the Newcastle Ottawa cohort scale was used for cross-­ sectional research (online supplemental file 1)
elements.reason: A modification is mentioned and referenced to a supplemental file, but the specific adaptations are not described in the text.
No newly developed risk-of-bias tool was used; an existing tool (modified NOS) was applied.

elements.quote: Each included study was independently reviewed for critical appraisal and bias reduction ... Consensus was used to settle disagreements
elements.reason: Independent assessment by reviewers and consensus-based disagreement resolution are reported, though the exact number of reviewers for appraisal is implied rather than stated.
No evidence of contacting investigators to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information; author contact was only for missing outcome data.
No automation tools were used for risk-of-bias assessment.

elements.quote: The effect size of each study was evaluated using the odds ratio (OR) and its 95% confidence interval (CI).
elements.reason: The Methods explicitly specify the odds ratio with 95% CI as the effect measure for the single outcome (association between MedDiet adherence and MetS), used consistently in the meta-analysis.

No thresholds or ranges for interpreting the effect size (e.g., magnitude of OR) or their rationale are reported; only I² heterogeneity interpretation cut-offs are given, which do not address effect size interpretation.
No methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure are described; the OR is used throughout without conversion methods reported.
The choice of the odds ratio as effect measure is stated but no justification or rationale for this choice is provided.

elements.quote: However, to narrow the scope of the meta-­ analysis, only studies that associated the MedDiet with the outcome of MetS were included.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the eligibility criteria for the review and explicitly states the process used to decide which studies were eligible for the meta-analysis (only studies associating MedDiet with MetS were included; duplicate data resolved by selecting the larger sample). Since there is a single synthesis (the meta-analysis), this adequately covers the requirement.

elements.quote: In cases where missing information was identified in the published paper, the relevant authors of those studies were contacted directly to request the missing information.
elements.reason: Handling of missing data is described (contacting authors for missing information), but methods for data conversions are not described in the Methods section; data conversion is only mentioned as a limitation in the Discussion ('the need to convert data for the purpose of quantitative analysis presents an additional limitation') without explaining how conversions were performed.
Tables exist (Table 1 critical appraisal, Table 2 study characteristics), but the Methods section contains no description of tabular structures used to display results or the data included in them.

elements.quote: Publication bias was assessed via a funnel plot, and Egger's test was used for the assessment of bias.
elements.reason: The Methods describe a funnel plot for displaying publication bias results, but there is no description of other graphical displays (e.g., forest plot in figure 2, sensitivity analysis figure 4) in the Methods.
No basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs (e.g., by weight, year, or effect size) is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
Only standard graphs (forest plot, funnel plot, sensitivity analysis plot) are used; no non-standard graphs are evident, so no rationale is required.

elements.quote: All analyses were conducted using Stata version 17.0 (StataCorp, College Station, TX, USA).
elements.reason: Software package and version number for the meta-analysis are explicitly reported.
A meta-analysis was performed, so no alternative synthesis method needed to be described.

elements.quote: the random-­ effects inverse variance model with the traditional DerSimonian and Laird method was used
elements.reason: The random-effects model is named; rationale is implicit in the choice of random-effects for heterogeneous studies but the model itself is clearly reported.

elements.quote: To determine the overall estimated OR and its related 95% CIs, the random-­ effects inverse variance model with the traditional DerSimonian and Laird method was used.
elements.reason: The statistical method (inverse variance, DerSimonian and Laird) for pooling ORs and CIs is reported.

elements.quote: To measure the percentage of disparities across studies, we used the inconsistency index ( I 2 ), which was calculated with the Cochran Q statistic.
elements.reason: Heterogeneity assessment via I² and Cochran Q, including interpretation cut-offs, is described.

elements.quote: the traditional DerSimonian and Laird method was used
elements.reason: The DerSimonian and Laird method implies the between-study variance estimator used for the random-effects model.

elements.quote: To determine the overall estimated OR and its related 95% CIs, the random-­ effects inverse variance model with the traditional DerSimonian and Laird method was used.
elements.reason: 95% CIs are stated to be derived within the inverse variance/DL framework, but the specific CI calculation method is not detailed beyond this.
No additional random-effects implementation details beyond the DL estimator are required or reported; standard implementation is implied.
A frequentist (DerSimonian-Laird) meta-analysis was performed, not Bayesian, so priors do not apply.
No methods for handling statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study are described in the retrieved evidence.
All studies were included in the meta-analysis; no planned syntheses were abandoned, so no reasons needed reporting.

elements.quote: To measure the percentage of disparities across studies, we used the inconsistency index ( I 2 ), which was calculated with the Cochran Q statistic.
elements.reason: The methods report only quantifying heterogeneity (I², Cochran Q); no methods to explore causes of heterogeneity (subgroup analysis, meta-regression) are described.
No subgroup analysis or meta-regression with factors, levels, or expected direction of effect modification is reported.
No heterogeneity-exploration analyses are reported, so whether study-level variables or within-study contrasts were used is not stated.
No subgroup analyses were performed, so no methods for comparing subgroup effects are reported.
No informal narrative exploration of heterogeneity with factors and levels is described in the methods.
No heterogeneity-exploration analyses are reported at all, so none are identified as post hoc or pre-specified.

elements.quote: We identified 3775 articles by searching the databases MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase (Ovid) and Web of Science. A total of 1456 studies were excluded because of duplication, while 1565 were classified as ineligible by automation tools. Another 546 studies were removed for additional reasons. We examined the titles and abstracts of 208 studies and excluded 157 on the basis of our findings.
elements.reason: Reports records identified (3775), duplicates removed (1456), automation-tool exclusions (1565), other removals (546), screened (208), and excluded at initial screening (157).

elements.quote: We screened 51 articles for eligibility. Eight studies were included in the meta-­ analysis.
elements.reason: Reports 51 articles assessed for eligibility and 8 included, but does not report the number of reports sought/not retrieved, nor the number excluded at full-text stage with primary reasons.
